rounds.text: Supreme Power Equipment Ltd exhibits robust fundamental performance, demonstrated by superior returns on capital employed of 20.73% and return on equity of 18.72%, both outpacing their respective sector benchmarks [E9, E10]. Revenue visibility is exceptionally strong, backed by a current order book of ₹565.80 Cr and H1 order wins totaling ₹209.24 Cr [E77, E78], which aligns with management's guidance for a minimum 30% year-on-year rise in revenue [E67]. Furthermore, intrinsic valuation metrics derived from discounted cash flow analysis place intrinsic value at ₹343 per share against the market price of ₹240, offering a tangible 30.0% margin of safety [E36, E37]. Operational efficiency has also seen structural enhancements, with debtor days dropping from 139 to 94.1 days and working capital requirements contracting significantly from 94.0 days to 39.1 days [E50, E51]. Conceded: the dividend yield sits at 0.00% [E4], and foreign and domestic institutional holdings have experienced declines from their December 2023 levels [E33, E34].

As the bear, I must highlight that Supreme Power Equipment Ltd carries notable valuation and structural risks that the headline multiples obscure. The company trades at a premium P/E of 25.63x and an EV/EBITDA of 16.34x, both of which sit above their respective sector benchmarks of 22.54x and 12.51x [E6, E11]. Furthermore, despite reporting profits, the company offers a dividend yield of 0.00% and does not pay out any dividends to its shareholders [E4, E52]. Balance sheet pressures are also mounting, with borrowings increasing to Rs 57 Cr in September 2026 from Rs 50 Cr a year earlier [E30], and the business generating a negative free cash flow of Rs -32 Cr as of March 2026 [E27]. Operational risks are further underlined by a heavy annualised volatility of 71.2% and a stark historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -74.2% [E44, E45]. Finally, institutional confidence has eroded dramatically, evidenced by foreign institutional holdings tumbling from 9.21% in December 2023 to just 0.75% in September 2026, alongside domestic institutional holdings dropping from 11.31% to 0.23% over the same period [E33, E34]. Conceded: the company displays strong short-term sales and profit growth alongside healthy order book visibility [E15, E17, E78], and management has provided encouraging revenue guidance for the year [E83].

The bear's concern over premium valuation multiples is offset by superior capital efficiency, as demonstrated by an ROE of 18.72% and ROCE of 20.73% that comfortably outpace sector benchmarks of 10.85% and 12.93% [E9, E10]. Conceded: the dividend yield is 0.00% [E4], but this reflects cash retention to fuel aggressive expansion, including a tank manufacturing facility capex of ₹20 to ₹22 crores and the ramp-up of the Kannur plant [E71, E72]. While borrowings rose to Rs 57 Cr and free cash flow was negative at Rs -32 Cr [E27, E30], working capital requirements have significantly compressed from 94.0 days to 39.1 days alongside a cash conversion ratio of 1.24x where profits are fully backed by cash [E25, E51]. The historical volatility and drawdown cited [E44, E45] ignore current technical strength where the price sits above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with a relative-strength rating of 100 [E41, E42]. Finally, the decline in institutional holdings [E33, E34] is directly countered by positive money flow and a promoter stake increase to 57.16% [E32, E35], while the robust order book of ₹565.80 Cr provides undeniable revenue visibility [E78].

Conceded: the company displays an ROE of 18.72% and ROCE of 20.73% that exceed sector benchmarks [E9, E10], alongside promoter stake rising to 57.16% and positive money flow [E32, E35]. However, the bull's dismissal of valuation ignores that the P/E of 25.63x and EV/EBITDA of 16.34x both trade at premiums to sector benchmarks of 22.54x and 12.51x [E6, E11]. Furthermore, defending zero dividends [E4] as mere capital retention for the Kannur ramp-up and the ₹20 to ₹22 crore tank facility [E71, E72] glosses over the severe negative free cash flow of Rs -32 Cr and rising borrowings reaching Rs 57 Cr [E27, E30]. While working capital days improved [E51], the current ratio sits at a thin buffer of 1.28x [E29] while foreign and domestic institutional holdings have collapsed by 8.46 and 11.08 percentage points respectively [E33, E34]. Finally, pointing to a relative-strength rating of 100 and moving averages [E41, E42] fails to mitigate the historical reality of a devastating -74.2% peak-to-trough drawdown and 71.2% annualised volatility [E44, E45].

Conceded: foreign and domestic institutional holdings have dropped by 8.46 and 11.08 percentage points [E33, E34], borrowings rose to ₹57 Cr [E30], free cash flow was negative at -₹32 Cr [E27], and the stock carries a high historical drawdown and volatility [E44, E45]. However, the bear's valuation critique ignores that a DCF model places intrinsic value at ₹343 per share against the market price of ₹240, offering a 30.0% margin of safety [E36, E37], while a reverse DCF shows the current price only prices in 13.1% growth versus the assumed 18.0% base case [E38]. Conceded: the P/E and EV/EBITDA trade at modest premiums to sector benchmarks [E6, E11], but these multiples are fully justified by superior profitability, featuring an ROE of 18.72% and ROCE of 20.73% that comfortably outpace sector medians [E9, E10], alongside robust sales growth of 46% TTM [E15]. The negative free cash flow reflects active capital deployment into growth drivers, specifically a ₹32 Cr CWIP for the Kannur facility ramp-up [E31, E71] and a tank facility expansion [E72], while operating cash flows remain robust at ₹26 Cr with profits fully backed by cash at 1.24x conversion [E25, E26]. Furthermore, institutional exits are offset by positive institutional money flow and rising promoter stakes to 57.16% [E32, E35], supported by a massive order book of ₹565.80 Cr providing high revenue visibility [E78].

Conceded: the DCF model places intrinsic value at ₹343 per share against the market price of ₹240 [E36, E37], and operating cash flow reached ₹26 Cr with a 1.24x cash conversion [E25, E26]. However, the bull's reliance on a 30% margin of safety and a reverse DCF implying 13.1% growth [E37, E38] overlooks the severe reality of a -₹32 Cr free cash flow [E27] and rising borrowings hitting ₹57 Cr [E30], which directly undermine the stability of those projected returns. Furthermore, while the bull defends the premium P/E of 25.63x and EV/EBITDA of 16.34x using strong ROE and ROCE metrics [E6, E9, E10, E11], these valuation multiples ignore that the yearly operating-margin trend is flagged as inconsistent [E23], and margins are already facing pressure from higher input costs and an inflationary environment [E74]. The bull points to a massive order book of ₹565.80 Cr [E78], but ignores that institutional exodus is extreme, with foreign and domestic institutional holdings having collapsed by 8.46 and 11.08 percentage points respectively [E33, E34]. Finally, the capital deployment into CWIP and facility expansion [E31, E71, E72] does not excuse the complete lack of dividend payouts [E52], leaving minority shareholders entirely exposed to high annualised volatility of 71.2% and a historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -74.2% [E44, E45].
